pageSubtitle: Shows where drivers are while they're out on a trip

gap.heading: Live tracking isn't available yet
gap.body: This page is meant to show where each driver is while a trip is on the road. That requires driver apps to continuously send their location during a delivery run — and today, they don't. Right now the system only records a handful of one-time locations, like where a stop was completed or where a trip began and ended. There's no ongoing stream of positions to plot on a map.

ready.heading: Where tracking will start
ready.body: One part of this is already solid and working today: the moment a dispatcher hands a trip's goods to a driver and the driver confirms receiving them, the system records that handover precisely. That moment — custody accepted — is the natural starting line for live tracking. Once location data starts flowing, this is the point where a driver will first appear on this map.

technical.body: The trip GPS-submission route that looks like it should power this validates incoming location data and discards it without saving — nothing is stored. There's no location-history record behind it either, only isolated coordinates tied to specific delivery events, like a stop or a trip's start and end point. The driver custody-acceptance boundary — the trip status this page already treats as "Custody Accepted" — is fully built and is the right trigger for tracking to begin once location data exists.

canvas.caption: The live map will render here once driver location data is available
